principles: Current and future product identities are Proof-or-Stop only.
Past proof bytes are evidence, not branding copy, and remain unchanged where verification depends on exact bytes.
The allowlist is exact, reasoned, mutation-tested, and rejects stale or broadened entries.
RED precedes every production migration and GREEN must be a descendant commit proving the same acceptance target.
drivers: Pre-public clean break explicitly requested by both maintainers.
Active bilingual compatibility creates ambiguity across packages, CLI, agents, env, paths, and docs.
Blind replacement can invalidate historical signatures and provenance.
Package tarballs and clean installs are the true external product boundary.

options.name: Clean break with exact historical allowlist
cons: Requires exact frozen-byte classification and migration tests

options.name: Keep additive read-both compatibility
pros: Lowest migration risk for old installs

chosen: Clean break with exact historical allowlist
rationale: Before public release, active compatibility has no customer value and directly contradicts the requested product experience. We will remove legacy package/bin/role/env/path/config/identifier surfaces, while freezing only exact historical or cryptographic bytes. The first DEV changes are the superseding decision and a committed failing acceptance harness; production edits follow only after RED is recorded.

preMortem.scenario: A broad replacement changes signature salts or historical story bytes
preMortem.trigger: Residue sweep reports zero because protected evidence was rewritten
preMortem.consequence: Persisted artifacts become unverifiable or audit history is falsified
preMortem.mitigation: Capture named pre-migration byte/digest/signature baselines; exact allowlist; assert unchanged after GREEN

preMortem.scenario: A deprecated bin or @lattice package survives in a packed artifact
preMortem.trigger: Source checks pass but clean install still resolves old identity
preMortem.consequence: Users see a bilingual product despite the cutover
preMortem.mitigation: Pack all packages, install tarballs in an empty temp project, assert canonical positives and legacy negatives

preMortem.scenario: Canonical source still writes legacy env/path/role/config names indirectly
preMortem.trigger: A resolver alias or generated template reintroduces Lattice on new writes
preMortem.consequence: Fresh projects and agents keep emitting retired identities
preMortem.mitigation: Test fresh generation and runtime writes, plus active-source residue scan and mutation proof

preMortem.scenario: The allowlist silently expands to hide new leaks
preMortem.trigger: A wildcard or stale exemption masks a new active occurrence
preMortem.mitigation: Require exact path/token/reason entries, fail on stale entries, and mutation-test an injected active leak

preMortem.trigger: Manifests change without synchronized lockfiles or version constant
preMortem.consequence: Builds or registry installs resolve inconsistent packages
preMortem.mitigation: Mechanical manifest/lock assertions, build all packages, pack inspection, clean-install smoke, and synchronized patch bump
